title: Outline of the 15th Five-Year Plan for National Economic and Social Development
institution: National People’s Congress; outline republished by Beijing Municipal People’s Congress
summary: The 2026–2030 outline places robotics among strategic emerging industries and embodied intelligence among future industries. It directs AI-plus adoption, model/algorithm work including embodied AI, and real-world application pilots; the text is a broad planning framework rather than an appropriated robotics program.
mechanism: Five-year national guidance: industrial prioritization, application demonstrations, future-industry pilots, and AI+ deployment.
limitations: The plan names eight strategic emerging industries and six future-industry fields across the relevant clauses; it does not establish an official “10 industry tracks” count. No robotics-specific quantified national target in the plan text located.

exact_quotes.quote: 推动量子科技、生物制造、氢能和核聚变能、脑机接口、具身智能、第六代移动通信等成为新的经济增长点。
加快新一代信息技术、新能源、新材料、智能网联新能源汽车、机器人、生物医药、高端装备、航空航天等战略性新兴产业发展

title: DeepSeek and Unitree Robotics: Examining the National Security Risks of PRC Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Autonomous Technologies and Building a Secure U.S. Technology Base
institution: House Homeland Security Committee, Subcommittee on Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Protection
summary: Confirmed hearing at 2 p.m. EDT, rescheduled from 10 a.m. The session examined PRC AI/robotics security and the U.S. technology base; official repository lists four public witnesses and their written statements.
mechanism: Oversight and public testimony; no legislation enacted by the hearing itself.
limitations: Repository has witness statements, not an official hearing transcript. An official livestream was announced; no official video/transcript artifact appeared in the repository checked.
transcript_availability: Official published GPO transcript (Serial 119-42, CHRG-119hhrg64201), full text saved. Written statements archived separately.

title: Robots Made in America: Advancing U.S. Leadership in Manufacturing and Automation
institution: House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, Subcommittee on Research and Technology
summary: The subcommittee examined U.S. robotics manufacturing and automation leadership. The official page identifies four witnesses and links written testimony; a livestream link is present, but the page/repository reviewed did not offer an official transcript.
mechanism: Policy oversight on manufacturing, workforce, innovation, adoption, and standards.
limitations: Witness claims are testimony, not committee findings; no official transcript located.

exact_quotes.quote: No country can win the AI race without also leading in robotics.

transcript_availability: No transcript entry in official House repository Event 119190 and none found in a targeted GovInfo search. Official video available; captions endpoint listed no tracks. Four prepared witness statements and hearing charter saved; these are not a transcript.

title: American Global Competitiveness at 250: Legislative Proposals to Secure U.S. Technology Leadership
institution: House Committee on Energy and Commerce, Subcommittee on Commerce, Manufacturing, and Trade
summary: The hearing considered a slate of technology and competitiveness bills, including H.R. 7334, the National Commission on Robotics Act. Four witnesses included Boston Dynamics chief legal officer Jason Fiorillo; it was not a robotics-only hearing.
mechanism: Legislative examination of proposed bills; hearing itself did not enact them.
limitations: The “10 industry tracks” framing is not corroborated here; the page lists multiple bills and broad technology competitiveness themes. Witness claims are advocacy/testimony.

exact_quotes.quote: H.R. 7334, National Commission on Robotics Act

transcript_availability: No transcript entry in official House repository Event 119423. Official video available; captions endpoint listed no tracks. Four prepared witness statements saved separately.

title: Legislative Hearing on Protecting Communications Networks and Improving Connectivity
institution: House Committee on Energy and Commerce, Subcommittee on Communications and Technology
summary: The subcommittee considered several communications bills, including H.R. 9129 (GUARD Act), which would direct scrutiny of foreign adversary robotics. Four witnesses were listed; AUVSI’s Michael Robbins was the robotics-relevant witness.
mechanism: Legislative hearing on proposals; GUARD Act at this point was proposed legislation.
limitations: The Select Committee press release describes a potential import prohibition in the proposed bill; that is not itself an FCC Covered List action or enacted restriction.
transcript_availability: Official unedited hearing transcript posted July 31, 2026 in House repository; full text saved. Prepared witness statements separately archived.

title: FCC Public Safety and Homeland Security Bureau Announces Addition of Foreign-Produced Power Inverters and Advanced Robotic Devices to FCC Covered List
summary: FCC added foreign-produced advanced robotic devices to its Covered List, except devices receiving DoW Conditional Approval. It relied on an Executive Branch interagency National Security Determination that such devices posed unacceptable national-security and U.S.-person safety/security risks.
mechanism: Secure Networks Act Section 2 / FCC equipment-authorization and subsidy restrictions, based on the Executive Branch interagency determination attached as Appendix C to DA 26-786. Covered devices include network-capable mobile ground robots; exclusions and Department of War conditional approval matter.
limitations: This is a device-category supply-chain/equipment authorization mechanism; it is separate from Commerce Section 232 import investigation. The September 2026 FCC notice later describes conditional approvals.

exact_quotes.quote: Foreign-produced advanced robotic devices, except advanced robotic devices which have been granted a Conditional Approval by DoW
pose an unacceptable risk to the national security of the United States and to the safety and security of U.S. persons

title: Notice of Request for Public Comments on Section 232 National Security Investigation of Imports of Robotics and Industrial Machinery
institution: U.S. Department of Commerce, Bureau of Industry and Security
summary: Commerce initiated a Section 232 investigation into national-security effects of imports of robotics and industrial machinery, parts and components. BIS requested public comments on domestic production, supply concentration, subsidies, import reliance, tariffs/quotas, employment and security risks.
mechanism: Trade Expansion Act Section 232 investigation under 19 U.S.C. §1862; distinct trade/import review potentially informing trade measures.
limitations: This is not the FCC Covered List action and does not itself establish the July 2026 foreign-produced advanced-device FCC restriction. Scope includes industrial machinery; excludes UAS.

exact_quotes.quote: On September 2, 2025, the Secretary of Commerce initiated an investigation under Section 232 (19 U.S.C. 1862)
